Flutter offers the best reachability potential, supporting iOS, Android, web, and 
desktop. Despite Android being a less popular operating system among British 
teens (Spence, 2016); the Android operating system offers strategic market 
advantages. Most notably within countries that use the IGCSE program, such as 
Argentina with the operating system dominating the market with a 90% share 
(statcounter, 2024; Cambridge International, 2024). Positioning both Flutter and 
Android Java as highly illusive options. 
While Swift, offers a highly complete feature set for native iOS development; it 
is highly limited in terms of its reachability among overseas students, and its 
learning-curve. The slower development time, and delay to development due to 
learning the Swift language and SwiftUI framework, make it a poor choice given 
the time constraints. 
Flutter proves itself as a strong contender for the rapid development capabilities, 
thanks to features like a single codebase, and hot reload. However, learning the 
framework and Dart, would significantly delay project development, which would 
pose a risk to development timelines. 
Android Java, on the contrary, is already familiar to the developer nullifying the 
learning curve required, enabling an immediate start to development. An earlier 
start is particularly tempting, due to risk reduction and the possibility for more 
features to be implemented. Additionally, Android Java’s large ecosystem, online 
resources, and community help further support its case. 
While Flutter offers better long-term viability for its rapid development times, 
and cross-platform capabilities; the time investment required for proficiency
